primary_field: migration ecology / information ecology / global-change phenology
primary_question: Does historical phenological predictability along a migration segment determine how strongly individual songbirds catch up to spring en route?

bird_dataset.citation: Nemes et al. 2024 Journal of Animal Ecology 93:294-306

phenology_predictability.source: USA National Phenology Network historical annual Spring Index First Leaf anomaly
phenology_predictability.period: 1981 through year before each focal migration year
phenology_predictability.primary_measure: Pearson correlation of annual first-leaf anomalies between paired south and north receiver cells
phenology_predictability.secondary_measure: prediction RMSE from north anomaly ~ south anomaly

prior_art_boundary: Kölzsch et al. 2015 showed that phenological predictability along goose routes can affect migration timing.
Bauer et al. 2020 developed theory linking environmental variability, information reliability and migration timing.
Nemes et al. 2024 showed that four songbird species catch up to spring during migration and explicitly stated that phenological predictability was not measured.
PAYOFF-B's preregistered Eurasian wigeon predictive-connectivity by incoming-phase correction interaction was not supported.
V7 does not claim that predictability, green-wave tracking, en-route adjustment or catch-up are new.

primary_estimands.south_lag: bird detection day at south receiver minus local actual spring-onset day
primary_estimands.north_lag: bird detection day at north receiver minus local actual spring-onset day
primary_estimands.recovery: south_lag - north_lag; positive values mean catch-up toward spring
primary_estimands.predictability: pre-outcome historical correlation of spring-onset anomalies between the individual's south and north receiver cells

first_allowed_outputs: presence and missingness of coordinates and required timing columns

primary_hypothesis.prediction: Higher pre-outcome phenological predictability is associated with greater reduction of south phenological lag by the north receiver.

primary_model: recovery ~ predictability + south_lag + route_distance + actual_green_wave_rate + species + year + (1|south_site) + (1|north_site)
secondary_model: north_lag ~ south_lag * predictability + route_distance + actual_green_wave_rate + species + year + site random effects; predicted south_lag:predictability interaction < 0
mandatory_sensitivities: Spearman rather than Pearson historical predictability
fixed pre-outcome historical window common to all birds
exclude route pairs with fewer than 20 historical years
first-leaf only primary; NDVI-based historical predictability only if independently reconstructable
US-only receiver pairs if USA-NPN historical raster coverage excludes Canadian northern receivers
control for migration distance and tracking year
cluster/route-pair robust uncertainty if mixed model is unstable

claim_ceiling.supported: Historical predictability along tracked route segments is associated with the degree to which songbirds close their phenological lag while migrating through North America.
not_licensed: proof that birds cognitively estimate correlation
reinterpretation of the preregistered wigeon null as support

reopen_or_stop_rule: If the schema gate fails, close V7 without lowering thresholds. If a post-2023 prior study is found to have already tested the same route-predictability moderation in these or comparable individual songbird data, stop for prior-art collision before outcome modeling.
